'''Zakya H. Kafafi'''  is an [[List of Egyptian Americans|Egyptian-American]] scientist who is a distinguished research fellow of the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department at [[Lehigh University]]. She was the first woman to be appointed to the [[National Science Foundation]] Director of the Division of Materials Research. At the US Naval Research Laboratory, she had established and led a section on organic optoelectronics. She carried out research on organic light-emitting materials and devices, and solar cells.

== Early life and education ==
Kafafi was born in [[Cairo, Egypt]] and went to a French private school called Lyçée Français du Caire with her two younger sisters.{{cn|date=August 2026}} She became interested in chemistry whilst she was at high school, and has said that her science teacher Monsieur Georges referred to her as "the chemist".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Zakya H. Kafafi - 2007 SPIE Women in Optics Planner|url=https://spie.org/about-spie/advocacy/women-in-optics/women-in-optics-planner/2007-wio-planner/kafafi-zakya-h|access-date=2020-08-25|website=spie.org}}</ref> She started her undergraduate degree in chemistry at the [[University of Houston]], where she minored in mathematics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=OSA Election Slate for 2019 Offices|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/leadership_and_volunteers/2019_election/election_bios/|access-date=2020-08-25|website=OSA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030044655/https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/leadership_and_volunteers/2019_election/election_bios/|archive-date=2020-10-30|url-status=dead}}</ref> She gave birth to her first child while she was a sophomore in college. She finished her undergraduate degree and moved to [[Rice University]] for graduate studies. While at Rice she gave birth to her second child and gained her MA and PhD in chemistry.<ref name=taz/> She worked on [[Low-Temperature Phenomena|low-temperature]] spectroscopy of high temperature materials using a technique called Matrix Isolation Spectroscopy. At Rice University, Kafafi was friends with one of the pioneers of Matrix Isolation [[Marilyn E. Jacox]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alumna's bequest supports young female scientists |date=26 October 2015 |url=https://chemistry.cornell.edu/news/alumnas-bequest-supports-young-female-scientists |access-date=2020-08-25 |publisher=Chemistry & Chemical Biology Cornell Arts & Sciences}}</ref> After completing her doctorate, Kafafi moved to [[Cairo]], where she was appointed assistant professor.{{citation needed|date=August 2020}} She returned to Houston Texas in 1981.{{cn|date=August 2026}}

== Research and career ==
In 1986, while still at Rice University, Kafafi learned about a position open in the Optical Sciences Division at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] (NRL).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lehigh CPN Faculty: Zakya H. Kafafi|url=https://www.lehigh.edu/~incpn/people/faculty/kafafi.html|access-date=2020-08-25|website=www.lehigh.edu|archive-date=2021-09-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210926170654/https://www.lehigh.edu/~incpn/people/faculty/kafafi.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kafafi eventually joined NRL, where she established the organic optoelectronics section.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Zakya Kafafi: Making a mark with materials |date = 7 February 2019|url=https://engineering.lehigh.edu/research/resolve/volume-1-2015/zakya-kafafi-making-mark-materials|access-date=2020-08-25 |publisher=P.C. Rossin College of Engineering & Applied Science}}</ref> She worked on nonlinear optical properties of organic and polymer materials using degenerate four wave mixing.<ref name=":1" /> She transitioned from chemical to materials and physical research, developing and studying the properties of [[OLED]]s.<ref name=taz>{{Cite journal|last=Taz|first=Humaira|date=2019|title=Zakya Kafafi: An international leader in materials research|journal=[[MRS Bulletin]] |volume=44 |issue=12 |pages=969–973 |doi=10.1557/mrs.2019.304 |issn=0883-7694|doi-access=free}}</ref> Kafafi spent over twenty years working at the NRL, during which time OLED displays found their way into flat panel display televisions and computers, mobile phones and watches.<ref name=":1" />

In 2007, Kafafi was appointed as [[National Science Foundation]] Director of the Division of Materials Research, during which time she oversaw a billion dollar budget.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Taz|first=Humaira|date=2019|title=Zakya Kafafi: An international leader in materials research|journal=MRS Bulletin|language=en|volume=44|issue=12|pages=969–973|doi=10.1557/mrs.2019.304|issn=0883-7694|doi-access=free}}</ref> She was the first woman to hold the position.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> In 2010, Kafafi visited Egypt, where she looked to develop partnerships that promoted solar energy across the country.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2010-05-19|title=Egypt's local initiatives with alternative energy|url=https://egyptindependent.com/egypts-local-initiatives-alternative-energy/|access-date=2020-08-25|website=Egypt Independent|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2008, Kafafi joined the faculty at [[Lehigh University]] first as an adjunct professor and later as  Distinguished Research Fellow in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering.<ref name=":3" /> She  developed metallic plasmonic nanostructures that can increase light absorption and the efficiency of organic photovoltaics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Solar panels as inexpensive as paint? It's possible due to research at UB, elsewhere|url=https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2013/05/018.html|access-date=2020-08-25|website=www.buffalo.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gan|first1=Qiaoqiang|last2=Bartoli|first2=Filbert J.|last3=Kafafi|first3=Zakya H.|date=2013|title=Plasmonic-Enhanced Organic Photovoltaics: Breaking the 10% Efficiency Barrier|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/adma.201203323|journal=Advanced Materials|language=en|volume=25|issue=17|pages=2385–2396|doi=10.1002/adma.201203323|pmid=23417974|bibcode=2013AdM....25.2385G |s2cid=13121924|issn=1521-4095|url-access=subscription}}</ref> These nanostructures make it possible to increase the optical absorption of the active layer of photovoltaics without increasing the layer thickness, allowing for improved device performance without compromising the flexibility or weight.<ref name=":3" />

In 2011, Kafafi established a journal for the International Sociery of Optics and Photonics. She was the Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Journal of Photonics for Energy]]'' for 10 years.{{citation needed|date=August 2022}} In 2014, Kafafi became the inaugural Deputy Editor of the sister journal to ''[[Science Advances]]''.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=AAAS Names Deputy Editors of Science Advances |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-names-deputy-editors-science-advances|access-date=2020-08-25 }}</ref>

Kafafi|url=https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/jurado/4402/|access-date=2020-08-25|website=Premios Fronteras|language=es}}</ref>
